Front:
A team needs a low-latency classifier that runs economically at high request volume and does not require broad world knowledge. Which model category should it evaluate first?

A) A small language model
B) A large reasoning model
C) A multimodal generation model
Back:
A) A small language model

Small language models can provide lower latency and cost for bounded tasks when their quality is sufficient.

Reference: Foundry model concepts
Extra: Use task fit rather than model size as the decision rule. Large reasoning models favor complex reasoning; multimodal generation is appropriate when image or audio generation is required. Benchmark quality, latency, and cost on representative data.

Front:
An app must answer questions about photographs and accompanying text in one request. Which model type best meets the requirement?

A) A text embedding model
B) A multimodal model
C) A speech synthesis model
Back:
B) A multimodal model

A multimodal model can jointly process visual and textual inputs for grounded responses.

Reference: Foundry model concepts
Extra: Embedding models encode similarity but do not independently reason over images. Speech synthesis produces audio. Multimodal models are selected when the task crosses input modalities such as text and vision.

Front:
A company wants grounded chat over policies with keyword matching, semantic similarity, filters, and managed indexing. Which service is the best fit?

A) Azure AI Search
B) Azure Blob Storage
C) Azure Cosmos DB
Back:
A) Azure AI Search

Azure AI Search provides managed indexing plus keyword, vector, hybrid, and semantic search capabilities.

Reference: Azure AI Search overview
Extra: Blob Storage is a content source, not a relevance engine. Cosmos DB can support vector workloads but does not provide the same integrated enrichment and semantic ranking toolchain. Search is the purpose-built grounding service.

Front:
A RAG workload must preserve exact product-code matches while also finding semantically similar passages. Which retrieval method should be selected?

A) Vector search only
B) Keyword search only
C) Hybrid search
Back:
C) Hybrid search

Hybrid search combines full-text and vector queries so exact tokens and semantic similarity both contribute.

Reference: Hybrid search overview
Extra: Keyword search protects exact identifiers; vector search captures conceptual similarity. Hybrid retrieval fuses both result sets, often followed by semantic ranking. It is preferable when neither lexical nor semantic evidence alone is sufficient.

Front:
Documents change hourly and answers must reflect updates quickly. Which indexing approach best reduces staleness without rebuilding everything?

A) Run scheduled incremental indexing
B) Recreate the full index monthly
C) Cache generated answers indefinitely
Back:
A) Run scheduled incremental indexing

Incremental indexing processes changed source content on a frequent schedule and limits unnecessary reprocessing.

Reference: Indexers overview
Extra: A monthly rebuild violates freshness, while an indefinite answer cache preserves stale facts. Use source change detection, indexing schedules, and freshness monitoring together; choose push ingestion when even shorter latency is required.

Front:
An agent needs durable conversation state shared across application instances. What should the architecture use?

A) Process-local variables
B) A persistent conversation store
C) Model parameters
Back:
B) A persistent conversation store

A persistent store keeps conversation state available across restarts and horizontally scaled instances.

Reference: Agent threads and messages
Extra: Process memory is ephemeral and instance-bound. Model parameters are not per-user memory. Keep identity-scoped state in a durable thread or data store, apply retention controls, and avoid placing sensitive data into prompts unnecessarily.

Front:
An agent must retrieve approved policy passages but must never update the source repository. Which integration design follows least privilege?

A) Grant repository-owner access
B) Grant read-only retrieval access
C) Embed administrator credentials
Back:
B) Grant read-only retrieval access

Read-only retrieval permissions provide the required knowledge while minimizing the agent blast radius.

Reference: Agent tools overview
Extra: Owner access exceeds the task, and embedded credentials create secret exposure. Treat tools as security boundaries: scope identities, validate arguments, restrict operations, and log calls independently of the model response.

Front:
A production AI application needs separate lifecycle management for prompts, evaluations, connections, and deployments. Which organizing construct should the team use?

A) A Foundry project
B) A storage container
C) A virtual machine scale set
Back:
A) A Foundry project

A Foundry project organizes AI development assets, connections, evaluations, and application workflows.

Reference: Microsoft Foundry overview
Extra: Storage containers hold objects but do not manage the AI lifecycle. VM scale sets manage compute. Projects provide a collaboration and governance boundary; use separate projects or environments where release isolation requires it.

Front:
A model endpoint has predictable sustained demand and requires reserved throughput with stable latency. Which deployment option is most appropriate?

A) Serverless API deployment
B) Provisioned deployment
C) Batch-only inference
Back:
B) Provisioned deployment

Provisioned deployment reserves model throughput for predictable, latency-sensitive production demand.

Reference: Azure OpenAI deployment types
Extra: Pay-as-you-go serverless deployment favors variable demand; batch inference favors asynchronous jobs. Provisioned capacity is justified by steady utilization and throughput assurance, not merely by a high short-lived peak.

Front:
A team evaluates several catalog models without managing hosting infrastructure and pays according to usage. Which option best fits?

A) Managed compute cluster
B) Self-hosted Kubernetes endpoint
C) Serverless API deployment
Back:
C) Serverless API deployment

Serverless API deployment exposes supported models without requiring the team to provision hosting infrastructure.

Reference: Deploy models as serverless APIs
Extra: Managed or self-hosted compute provides more infrastructure control but adds operations. Serverless endpoints accelerate model comparison and variable workloads; verify model, region, quota, and billing availability before selection.

Front:
A release pipeline must promote a tested prompt and agent configuration without manual portal edits. What should the team implement?

A) Versioned assets and automated deployment
B) Shared administrator portal sessions
C) Direct production-only experimentation
Back:
A) Versioned assets and automated deployment

Version control plus automated deployment makes promotion repeatable, reviewable, and auditable.

Reference: CI/CD for Foundry
Extra: Portal sessions are not reproducible, and production-only experiments bypass quality gates. Treat prompts, evaluations, infrastructure, and agent definitions as release artifacts with environment-specific configuration and rollback points.

Front:
A CI pipeline deploys to test and production. Production uses different endpoints and identities. How should configuration be handled?

A) Hard-code production values
B) Use environment-specific parameters
C) Copy values through chat messages
Back:
B) Use environment-specific parameters

Environment-specific parameters separate deployable logic from endpoint, identity, and connection values.

Reference: CI/CD for Foundry
Extra: Hard-coding impedes safe promotion; ad hoc copying is error-prone and unaudited. Keep secrets outside source control, use federated pipeline identity, and require the same validation gates in each environment.

Front:
Users receive throttling errors although the endpoint is healthy. Monitoring shows requests exceed the deployment token rate. What is the most direct action?

A) Increase quota or reduce request rate
B) Add more search documents
C) Disable content filtering
Back:
A) Increase quota or reduce request rate

Rate-limit failures require demand shaping, quota changes, or capacity changes rather than unrelated data or safety changes.

Reference: Azure OpenAI quotas and limits
Extra: Use bounded retries with server guidance, request queues, token budgeting, and regional capacity planning. Search corpus size and content filters do not increase the model deployment rate limit.

Front:
A chatbot cost spike is caused by repeatedly sending an entire long conversation. Which change most directly lowers token consumption while retaining relevant context?

A) Increase maximum output tokens
B) Summarize and trim conversation history
C) Duplicate the system prompt
Back:
B) Summarize and trim conversation history

Context summarization and selective history reduce input tokens while preserving information needed for the next turn.

Reference: Prompt engineering concepts
Extra: Higher output limits can increase cost, and duplicated instructions consume more tokens. Combine a context budget with retrieval and durable memory so only relevant state enters each model call.

Front:
A team must determine whether answer quality declined after a retrieval change. Which telemetry should it compare first?

A) VM disk utilization
B) Groundedness and retrieval relevance
C) Browser viewport dimensions
Back:
B) Groundedness and retrieval relevance

Groundedness and retrieval relevance directly reveal whether answers remain supported by useful retrieved evidence.

Reference: Foundry evaluators
Extra: Infrastructure telemetry can explain availability but not evidence quality. Segment evaluation by corpus, query class, and release; pair offline test sets with production traces to distinguish retrieval regressions from generation regressions.

Front:
An indexer completes successfully, but newly uploaded files never appear in search. Which operational check is most relevant?

A) Inspect ingestion status and source change detection
B) Increase model temperature
C) Modify speech output voice
Back:
A) Inspect ingestion status and source change detection

Indexer execution details and change-detection configuration identify skipped or failed source documents.

Reference: Monitor indexers
Extra: A successful top-level run can still include document-level warnings or unsupported changes. Generation and speech settings are downstream. Monitor document counts, failures, latency, and freshness separately.

Front:
An application running on Azure must call a model endpoint without storing keys. Which authentication method is preferred?

A) Managed identity with RBAC
B) A key committed to source
C) A shared key in the prompt
Back:
A) Managed identity with RBAC

Managed identity and role-based access provide keyless authentication with centrally scoped permissions.

Reference: Azure AI services authentication
Extra: Keys in code or prompts can leak and are difficult to scope. Assign only the data-plane role required, separate deployment management from inference, and use workload identity for supported non-Azure hosts.

Front:
A regulated workload requires model traffic to remain on private network paths and public endpoint access to be blocked. Which design is appropriate?

A) Public endpoint with a complex key
B) Private endpoint with public access disabled
C) Browser-side endpoint invocation
Back:
B) Private endpoint with public access disabled

A private endpoint provides private addressability; disabling public access closes the public network path.

Reference: Configure private networking
Extra: Authentication alone does not provide network isolation, and browser invocation exposes the endpoint surface. Plan private DNS and connectivity for developers, pipelines, tools, and dependent services.

Front:
A security team must block a known list of prohibited internal project names in model inputs and outputs. Which control is most targeted?

A) A custom blocklist
B) A token rate limit
C) A semantic search profile
Back:
A) A custom blocklist

A custom blocklist targets organization-specific terms in content filtering flows.

Reference: Use a custom blocklist
Extra: Rate limits control volume, not content. Search profiles rank documents. Blocklists are deterministic term controls and should complement, not replace, category filters and broader data-loss prevention.

Front:
A RAG system ingests untrusted webpages containing instructions aimed at overriding the system prompt. Which protection directly addresses this risk?

A) Prompt Shields for documents
B) A larger embedding dimension
C) A lower search replica count
Back:
A) Prompt Shields for documents

Prompt Shields can detect indirect prompt attacks embedded in third-party documents used for grounding.

Reference: Prompt Shields
Extra: Embedding size and replica count do not classify malicious instructions. Also isolate retrieved data from trusted instructions, constrain tools, validate outputs, and avoid granting the model unnecessary authority.

Front:
Before releasing an agent, a team needs repeatable measurements of harmful-content risk on a representative dataset. What should it run?

A) Safety evaluations
B) DNS resolution tests
C) Storage throughput tests
Back:
A) Safety evaluations

Safety evaluators quantify relevant content and security risks against a controlled evaluation dataset.

Reference: Risk and safety evaluators
Extra: Network and storage tests are operational checks, not behavioral safety evidence. Establish release thresholds, retain datasets and evaluator versions, and supplement automated metrics with human review for high-impact use cases.

Front:
Auditors must reconstruct which sources and tool calls contributed to an agent decision. Which implementation provides the strongest evidence?

A) Trace logging with provenance metadata
B) Aggregate request counts only
C) A screenshot of the final answer
Back:
A) Trace logging with provenance metadata

Traces and provenance connect a response to retrieval results, prompts, model calls, and tool activity.

Reference: Foundry observability
Extra: Counts lack per-run causality, while screenshots omit hidden steps. Protect logs as sensitive data, apply retention and redaction, and correlate traces with deployment and prompt versions.

Front:
An expense agent may prepare reimbursements but payments above a threshold require a person to approve execution. Which control should be implemented?

A) Human approval before the payment tool
B) Higher model temperature for exceptions
C) Automatic retries until payment succeeds
Back:
A) Human approval before the payment tool

A human-in-the-loop approval gate constrains high-impact tool execution while allowing lower-risk automation.

Reference: Human-in-the-loop workflows
Extra: Temperature changes randomness, not authorization. Automatic retries can amplify harm. Place deterministic policy checks outside the model and record the approver, decision, arguments, and resulting action.

Front:
An agent needs only calendar availability but its connector can also delete events. What is the best governance action?

A) Give the agent the full connector
B) Expose a read-only availability tool
C) Rely on the system prompt alone
Back:
B) Expose a read-only availability tool

A narrowly scoped tool schema and identity enforce least privilege beyond prompt instructions.

Reference: Agent tools overview
Extra: Prompts are not authorization boundaries. Avoid exposing unused destructive operations, validate all tool arguments server-side, and separate read and write identities where practical.

Front:
A deployment serves users in several regions and one region reaches quota. Which plan best improves resilience?

A) Route across independently provisioned regional deployments
B) Put all quota in the saturated region
C) Remove client retry limits
Back:
A) Route across independently provisioned regional deployments

Regional deployments with health- and capacity-aware routing reduce dependence on one regional quota pool.

Reference: Deployment options
Extra: Concentrating quota preserves the single bottleneck. Unbounded retries worsen overload. Confirm data residency, model availability, quota, and failover behavior for every target region.

Front:
A team wants alerts when a new prompt version increases latency and token use. Which observability design is most useful?

A) Trace model calls with version and token attributes
B) Record only monthly Azure cost totals
C) Sample only successful HTTP status codes
Back:
A) Trace model calls with version and token attributes

Per-call traces linked to prompt versions support latency breakdowns, token analysis, and regression detection.

Reference: Foundry observability
Extra: Monthly totals are too coarse and success-only sampling hides failures. Track retrieval, model, and tool spans; define service-level indicators and redact sensitive prompt content.

Front:
A public-facing agent can propose actions with legal impact. Which operating mode best manages risk during initial rollout?

A) Fully autonomous execution
B) Semiautonomous with approvals
C) Unlogged background execution
Back:
B) Semiautonomous with approvals

Semiautonomous operation adds human oversight at consequential boundaries while collecting evidence for later tuning.

Reference: Human-in-the-loop workflows
Extra: Autonomy should be earned through measured reliability and bounded impact. Unlogged operation prevents audit and learning. Define escalation, timeout, override, and rollback behavior before expanding autonomy.

Front:
A team must compare two model deployments while holding prompts and test cases constant. Which method yields defensible results?

A) Run both against the same evaluation dataset
B) Compare unrelated production anecdotes
C) Compare catalog descriptions only
Back:
A) Run both against the same evaluation dataset

A shared representative dataset and common evaluators isolate model differences and support repeatability.

Reference: Evaluate generative AI apps
Extra: Anecdotes and catalog text do not control inputs. Track model and evaluator versions, confidence intervals, latency, cost, safety, and task quality rather than relying on one aggregate score.

Front:
A Python application must use project connections and deployed assets consistently across environments. What should it use?

A) Foundry SDK with project configuration
B) Screen scraping the Foundry portal
C) Hard-coded browser cookies
Back:
A) Foundry SDK with project configuration

The SDK provides supported programmatic access to project-scoped resources and connections.

Reference: Foundry SDK overview
Extra: Portal scraping and cookies are brittle and insecure. Externalize project endpoint and deployment names, authenticate with token credentials, and use separate identities per environment.

Front:
A support assistant must answer only from approved manuals and cite the retrieved passages. Which pattern should be implemented?

A) Retrieval-augmented generation
B) Unconstrained model completion
C) Image generation with a mask
Back:
A) Retrieval-augmented generation

RAG retrieves approved evidence and supplies it to generation so answers can be grounded and cited.

Reference: RAG overview
Extra: An unconstrained completion relies on model memory and cannot guarantee source support. Image masking is unrelated. Enforce source scope, include citation metadata, and evaluate both retrieval relevance and groundedness.

Front:
A RAG assistant retrieves relevant documents but often misses the exact paragraph needed. Which change should be tested first?

A) Improve chunking and overlap
B) Increase speech recognition timeout
C) Add an image watermark
Back:
A) Improve chunking and overlap

Chunk boundaries and overlap strongly affect whether retrievable units preserve the evidence needed to answer a query.

Reference: Chunk documents for vector search
Extra: Oversized chunks dilute similarity and consume context; tiny chunks lose context. Speech and watermark settings do not affect text retrieval. Evaluate chunking with real questions rather than selecting size by intuition alone.

Front:
A workflow must extract an order, validate inventory through an API, and request approval before submission. Which design is best?

A) A multistep tool-augmented workflow
B) A single embedding operation
C) A static text completion only
Back:
A) A multistep tool-augmented workflow

A multistep workflow can sequence extraction, deterministic API validation, approval, and submission.

Reference: Foundry Agent Service overview
Extra: Embeddings do not execute business processes, and a static completion cannot verify live inventory. Keep deterministic validation outside free-form generation and make submission idempotent.

Front:
An application needs generated output that downstream code can validate against fixed fields and types. Which approach is most suitable?

A) Structured JSON output with a schema
B) Free-form prose with parsing heuristics
C) A vector embedding response
Back:
A) Structured JSON output with a schema

Schema-constrained structured output improves reliable machine parsing and field validation.

Reference: Structured outputs
Extra: Free-form parsing is fragile, while embeddings are numerical representations rather than extracted records. Still validate business rules server-side because schema conformance does not prove factual correctness.

Front:
A model response is fluent but asserts facts absent from the supplied evidence. Which evaluator most directly detects the issue?

A) Groundedness evaluator
B) Network latency metric
C) Index storage size
Back:
A) Groundedness evaluator

Groundedness measures whether response claims are supported by the provided context.

Reference: Foundry evaluators
Extra: Latency and storage are operational measures. Groundedness differs from relevance: a response can address the question yet introduce unsupported claims. Review retrieved evidence when groundedness declines.

Front:
A team must evaluate whether an answer directly addresses the user question, independent of citation support. Which dimension should it measure?

A) Response relevance
B) Replica utilization
C) Audio word error rate
Back:
A) Response relevance

Response relevance assesses how well an answer addresses the query rather than whether it is supported by context.

Reference: Evaluate generative AI apps
Extra: Groundedness and relevance are complementary: one checks support, the other checks usefulness to the query. Replica utilization and speech error rate concern different system layers.

Front:
A model performs well on average but fails on safety-critical edge cases. How should the evaluation dataset be improved?

A) Add representative adversarial and boundary cases
B) Remove all low-scoring examples
C) Keep only the shortest prompts
Back:
A) Add representative adversarial and boundary cases

Targeted edge and adversarial cases expose failures that averages over routine examples can hide.

Reference: Evaluation guidance
Extra: Removing failures biases the benchmark; prompt length alone is not risk coverage. Segment results by scenario and severity, and block release when critical thresholds fail even if the mean is high.

Front:
A developer is configuring an application to use a Foundry project. Which values should be externalized instead of embedded in business logic?

A) Project endpoint and deployment name
B) User questions and model answers
C) Retrieved chunks and citations
Back:
A) Project endpoint and deployment name

Project and deployment identifiers are environment configuration and should be injected at deployment time.

Reference: Foundry SDK overview
Extra: User content and retrieval results are runtime data, not deployment configuration. Externalization supports promotion across environments and avoids source edits; authenticate separately with managed credentials.

Front:
An assistant must call a weather API with a city and date. What makes the function tool safest and most reliable?

A) A narrow typed schema with validated arguments
B) An unrestricted shell command string
C) A broad administrator API token
Back:
A) A narrow typed schema with validated arguments

A typed, constrained tool schema helps the model form valid calls and enables server-side validation.

Reference: Function calling
Extra: Shell strings invite injection, and administrator tokens violate least privilege. Treat model-produced arguments as untrusted, constrain destinations and time ranges, and return structured errors.

Front:
An agent must preserve a user's multi-turn context while keeping different users isolated. Which approach should be used?

A) A separate thread per conversation
B) One global thread for all users
C) A shared system prompt as memory
Back:
A) A separate thread per conversation

Conversation-scoped threads preserve message history while supporting isolation between users and sessions.

Reference: Threads, runs, and messages
Extra: A global thread risks data leakage, and a system prompt is instruction, not durable user state. Authorize thread access and define retention, summarization, and deletion policies.

Front:
An agent needs current product facts from a search index and calculations from an internal pricing API. Which tool design is appropriate?

A) Add retrieval and function tools
B) Fine-tune on current prices only
C) Put all prices in the system prompt
Back:
A) Add retrieval and function tools

Retrieval supplies current knowledge while function calling invokes authoritative calculations.

Reference: Agent tool catalog
Extra: Fine-tuning is not a live data synchronization mechanism, and prompt-embedded prices become stale. Separate read-only evidence retrieval from transactional or computational tools.

Front:
A customer-service agent may issue refunds only after checking order status and policy eligibility. Where should eligibility enforcement occur?

A) In deterministic tool-side validation
B) Only in natural-language instructions
C) By increasing retrieval top-k
Back:
A) In deterministic tool-side validation

Tool-side authorization and business validation enforce policy even when model output is incorrect or manipulated.

Reference: Agent tools overview
Extra: Prompts guide behavior but do not enforce authorization. Retrieval depth affects evidence, not execution rights. Require idempotency, limits, audit logs, and approval for exceptional refunds.

Front:
A complex request requires a research specialist, a compliance reviewer, and a final writer with clear handoffs. Which architecture fits best?

A) An orchestrated multi-agent workflow
B) One embedding model invocation
C) A single static search query
Back:
A) An orchestrated multi-agent workflow

An orchestrator can assign bounded roles, pass artifacts, and enforce review before final composition.

Reference: Multi-agent workflows
Extra: Embeddings and static queries are components, not role coordination. Use multiple agents only when specialization and controlled handoffs outweigh added latency, cost, and debugging complexity.

Front:
Two agents repeatedly delegate the same task to each other. Which fix most directly prevents the loop?

A) Add termination conditions and handoff limits
B) Increase each agent's temperature
C) Remove all trace correlation IDs
Back:
A) Add termination conditions and handoff limits

Explicit stop criteria, turn budgets, and allowed handoff rules bound orchestration loops.

Reference: Multi-agent workflows
Extra: More randomness does not ensure termination, and removing traces makes diagnosis harder. Include a fallback path when confidence, tool errors, or budget thresholds are reached.

Front:
An autonomous procurement workflow can draft an order but must not submit purchases over a fixed amount. Which safeguard is strongest?

A) A deterministic amount check plus approval gate
B) A reminder in the user interface
C) A higher maximum token setting
Back:
A) A deterministic amount check plus approval gate

A code-enforced threshold and approval gate prevent unauthorized high-value execution.

Reference: Human-in-the-loop workflows
Extra: UI reminders are advisory and token limits control response length. Enforce policy at the tool boundary, record approvals, and use idempotency keys to prevent duplicate orders.

Front:
An agent's production failures are difficult to reproduce because only final responses are logged. What telemetry should be added?

A) Correlated traces for model, retrieval, and tool spans
B) Daily screenshots of the chat interface
C) Aggregate storage capacity charts
Back:
A) Correlated traces for model, retrieval, and tool spans

End-to-end traces expose intermediate inputs, outputs, timing, and errors for each agent step.

Reference: Foundry observability
Extra: Screenshots and capacity charts omit execution causality. Include deployment, prompt, and tool versions, but redact secrets and sensitive content before export.

Front:
A deployed agent suddenly starts choosing the wrong tool after a schema update. What should error analysis compare first?

A) Tool-call traces before and after the schema change
B) Search service disk capacity only
C) The browser's preferred language
Back:
A) Tool-call traces before and after the schema change

Comparing tool selection, arguments, and errors across versions isolates schema-related behavior changes.

Reference: Foundry observability
Extra: Infrastructure capacity and browser locale are weak hypotheses unless traces indicate them. Maintain versioned schemas and replay representative traces in a test environment before promotion.

Front:
A creative writing feature produces repetitive text. Which parameter adjustment generally increases output diversity?

A) Increase temperature moderately
B) Set temperature to zero
C) Reduce retrieval replicas
Back:
A) Increase temperature moderately

Higher temperature generally broadens token sampling and can increase variation in generated text.

Reference: Azure OpenAI inference reference
Extra: Temperature zero favors determinism, while search replicas do not change token sampling. Tune on task-specific evaluations; excessive randomness can reduce coherence and factual reliability.

Front:
A data-extraction task requires consistent outputs across repeated runs. Which generation setting is the better starting point?

A) A low temperature
B) A high temperature
C) A random tool schema
Back:
A) A low temperature

Lower temperature reduces sampling variability and is a better fit for deterministic extraction.

Reference: Azure OpenAI inference reference
Extra: High temperature favors diversity. Determinism also requires a precise schema, stable model version, controlled prompt, and validation; temperature alone does not guarantee identical results.

Front:
A prompt works on examples but fails when input includes instructions from an untrusted document. Which prompt design is safer?

A) Delimit data and state that it is untrusted
B) Concatenate data as system instructions
C) Grant the model broader tool access
Back:
A) Delimit data and state that it is untrusted

Separating instructions from untrusted content reduces instruction confusion and supports prompt-injection defenses.

Reference: Prompt engineering concepts
Extra: System-level concatenation elevates attacker text, and broader tools increase impact. Pair prompt structure with Prompt Shields, least privilege, output validation, and tool authorization.

Front:
A team wants a model to critique its draft before final output. Which pattern matches the requirement?

A) A self-critique or reflection loop
B) A one-pass embedding call
C) An index replica scale-out
Back:
A) A self-critique or reflection loop

A reflection loop asks the model or a reviewer model to assess and revise a draft against explicit criteria.

Reference: Prompt flow concepts
Extra: Embeddings encode text and replicas improve search availability. Reflection can improve quality but adds latency and cost, and correlated model errors mean it does not replace external evaluation.

Front:
A self-critique loop continues revising without meaningful improvement. Which control should be added?

A) A maximum iteration count and quality threshold
B) Unlimited recursive calls
C) A larger vector index
Back:
A) A maximum iteration count and quality threshold

Bounded iterations and explicit acceptance criteria prevent runaway cost and latency.

Reference: Prompt flow concepts
Extra: Unlimited recursion can amplify cost without quality gains; index size is unrelated. Log score changes per iteration and fall back to review when the threshold is not reached.

Front:
Operations needs to know whether latency comes from retrieval, model inference, or a downstream tool. Which instrumentation is required?

A) Separate correlated spans for each stage
B) One timer around the whole request
C) Monthly billing totals only
Back:
A) Separate correlated spans for each stage

Stage-level spans provide latency breakdowns while correlation preserves the end-to-end execution path.

Reference: Foundry observability
Extra: A total timer reveals a symptom but not the bottleneck; billing totals are even coarser. Capture retries, token counts, status, and versions on relevant spans.

Front:
A cost dashboard must attribute usage to application, model deployment, and feature. Which telemetry is most useful?

A) Token counts tagged with deployment and operation
B) A count of portal sign-ins
C) The number of index field names
Back:
A) Token counts tagged with deployment and operation

Tagged input and output token metrics support granular usage and cost attribution.

Reference: Foundry observability
Extra: Portal activity and schema field counts are not consumption measures. Combine token telemetry with request counts, cache behavior, latency, and pricing dimensions.

Front:
A router should send simple classification to a cheaper model and complex reasoning to a stronger model. Which architecture implements this?

A) A policy-based multi-model router
B) A single fixed model for every request
C) A search-only indexing pipeline
Back:
A) A policy-based multi-model router

A router can classify task complexity and direct requests to models that balance quality, latency, and cost.

Reference: Foundry models
Extra: A fixed model forfeits optimization, and indexing does not perform generation routing. Evaluate routing mistakes and include fallback when a selected model fails or lacks capability.

Front:
A workflow must apply exact tax rules and then generate a customer-friendly explanation. What design is best?

A) Rules engine for calculation plus LLM for explanation
B) LLM alone for tax calculation and explanation
C) Vector search alone for final calculation
Back:
A) Rules engine for calculation plus LLM for explanation

Deterministic rules enforce exact calculations, while the model handles natural-language presentation.

Reference: Foundry Agent Service overview
Extra: LLMs can be nondeterministic with arithmetic and policy enforcement; search retrieves information but does not execute tax rules. Preserve the calculated result as authoritative structured data.

Front:
A RAG application answers accurately offline but poorly in production because user queries differ from the test set. What is the best next step?

A) Curate evaluation cases from production traces
B) Remove production monitoring
C) Increase output length for every query
Back:
A) Curate evaluation cases from production traces

Privacy-safe production traces reveal real query distributions and failure modes for a representative benchmark.

Reference: Evaluate generative AI apps
Extra: Removing telemetry eliminates evidence, and longer answers do not fix distribution shift. Sample across segments, redact sensitive data, label failures, and preserve a stable holdout set.

Front:
An agent calls the same non-idempotent booking tool twice after a timeout. Which application control prevents duplicate reservations?

A) An idempotency key on the tool operation
B) A higher model temperature
C) More embedding dimensions
Back:
A) An idempotency key on the tool operation

An idempotency key lets retries resolve to the original operation instead of creating a second booking.

Reference: Idempotency pattern
Extra: Sampling and embedding settings do not provide transaction safety. Pair idempotency with bounded retries, status reconciliation, and durable records of tool outcomes.

Front:
A function tool returns a transient HTTP 429 response. How should the agent workflow handle it?

A) Use bounded retries with backoff
B) Retry immediately without a limit
C) Mark the call successful
Back:
A) Use bounded retries with backoff

Bounded exponential backoff respects transient throttling while limiting latency and retry amplification.

Reference: Transient fault handling
Extra: Unbounded immediate retries worsen throttling, while false success corrupts workflow state. Honor retry guidance, cap attempts, and expose a recoverable failure path.

Front:
A model should return no answer when retrieved evidence is insufficient. Which implementation is most reliable?

A) Define an abstention rule based on evidence quality
B) Force an answer with a longer prompt
C) Increase temperature until an answer appears
Back:
A) Define an abstention rule based on evidence quality

An explicit abstention policy lets the application decline when retrieval or groundedness signals are inadequate.

Reference: RAG overview
Extra: Forcing generation increases fabrication risk, and higher temperature adds variability. Calibrate thresholds on labeled cases and offer escalation or source-search alternatives.

Front:
A team changes its embedding model for an existing vector index. What must it plan to do?

A) Re-embed the corpus and queries consistently
B) Keep old document vectors with new query vectors
C) Convert vectors into speech audio
Back:
A) Re-embed the corpus and queries consistently

Document and query vectors must be generated in the same compatible embedding space for meaningful similarity.

Reference: Vector search overview
Extra: Mixing embedding spaces makes distance scores unreliable. Use a versioned parallel index for migration, evaluate retrieval, and switch traffic only after backfill completes.

Front:
A vector search index must restrict results to documents a user is authorized to view. Which design is required?

A) Apply identity-aware security filters during retrieval
B) Filter citations after model generation
C) Ask the model to ignore restricted text
Back:
A) Apply identity-aware security filters during retrieval

Retrieval-time authorization prevents unauthorized content from entering the model context.

Reference: Security trimming
Extra: Post-generation filtering is too late, and prompt instructions are not access control. Propagate trusted identity claims and test for cross-tenant leakage.

Front:
A service must generate a product image from a written description. Which capability should be selected?

A) Text-to-image generation
B) Speech-to-text transcription
C) Vector similarity search
Back:
A) Text-to-image generation

Text-to-image models synthesize visual content from natural-language prompts.

Reference: Azure OpenAI models
Extra: Speech transcription converts audio to text, and vector search retrieves existing items. Apply content policy, provenance, brand, and human-review controls to generated assets.

Front:
A designer must replace only the background of an existing image while preserving the foreground object. Which workflow is appropriate?

A) Mask-based inpainting
B) Full-image OCR
C) Speech synthesis
Back:
A) Mask-based inpainting

Inpainting uses a mask to identify the region that the image model should modify.

Reference: Image generation guidance
Extra: OCR reads text and speech synthesis creates audio. Carefully align mask semantics with the API, preserve the original asset, and evaluate edge blending and brand compliance.

Front:
A marketing team needs a short video created from a text storyboard and a reference image. Which model capability is required?

A) Video generation from text and media
B) Document layout extraction
C) Keyword-only search
Back:
A) Video generation from text and media

A supported video generation model can use textual direction and reference media to synthesize video.

Reference: Foundry model catalog
Extra: Layout extraction structures documents, and keyword search retrieves content. Verify model availability and use controls for duration, style, safety, provenance, and rights.

Front:
A generated video contains one incorrect segment that must be revised while the rest remains unchanged. What approach best fits?

A) Use a supported video-editing workflow
B) Rebuild the search index
C) Retrain a speech recognizer
Back:
A) Use a supported video-editing workflow

Video-editing controls target generated media modifications without involving unrelated search or speech services.

Reference: Foundry model catalog
Extra: Platform capabilities vary by model, so assess whether segment editing, reference conditioning, or regeneration is supported. Preserve provenance and review transitions around the edit.

Front:
An accessibility application needs a concise description of the essential content in a photograph. Which output should it request?

A) Alt text grounded in the image
B) An unrelated creative story
C) A vector index schema
Back:
A) Alt text grounded in the image

Grounded alt text communicates essential visual information for users who cannot access the image directly.

Reference: Image descriptions
Extra: Creative prose may invent details and an index schema does not describe content. Keep alt text concise, contextual, and free of redundant phrases; use extended descriptions only when complexity warrants them.

Front:
A museum image contains a complex chart that cannot be explained concisely. Which accessibility output is most suitable?

A) An extended image description
B) A one-word sentiment label
C) A speech recognition transcript
Back:
A) An extended image description

Extended descriptions provide the detail and structure needed for complex visual information.

Reference: Image descriptions
Extra: A short alt-text field may identify the chart and point to the longer description. Sentiment and transcription do not convey axes, trends, annotations, and relationships.

Front:
A claims app must answer questions about visible vehicle damage and cite what can be seen in the uploaded image. Which approach should it use?

A) Multimodal visual question answering
B) Text-only keyword matching
C) Audio speaker identification
Back:
A) Multimodal visual question answering

A multimodal model can reason over the image and question to produce an answer grounded in visual evidence.

Reference: Vision analysis concepts
Extra: Keyword search cannot inspect pixels and speaker identification concerns audio. Require uncertainty handling and human review because visual evidence may be incomplete or ambiguous.

Front:
A pipeline must extract visual characteristics from mixed documents and media into structured fields. Which Foundry Tool is designed for this?

A) Azure Content Understanding
B) Azure DNS
C) Azure Load Testing
Back:
A) Azure Content Understanding

Content Understanding analyzes multimodal content and produces structured outputs using configured analyzers.

Reference: Content Understanding overview
Extra: DNS resolves names and Load Testing measures application performance. Define a schema aligned to downstream decisions and validate extracted values against representative content.

Front:
A developer needs a quick predefined extraction for one focused media task rather than a customizable end-to-end analyzer. Which Content Understanding mode is the better starting point?

A) Single-task mode
B) Pro mode
C) Search replica mode
Back:
A) Single-task mode

Single-task mode targets a focused predefined operation with less configuration.

Reference: Content Understanding overview
Extra: Pro mode is appropriate when custom schemas and richer processing are needed. Search replicas scale query serving and are not Content Understanding pipeline modes.

Front:
A custom media workflow needs schema-driven extraction across multiple content types and richer control. Which Content Understanding mode should be chosen?

A) Pro mode
B) Single-task mode
C) Keyword analyzer mode
Back:
A) Pro mode

Pro mode supports configurable, schema-oriented multimodal analysis for more complex workflows.

Reference: Content Understanding overview
Extra: Single-task mode is simpler but less adaptable. A keyword analyzer is a search text-processing concept, not the rich multimodal analyzer requested.

Front:
A security system must identify objects and their locations within each frame, not merely describe the whole image. Which output is required?

A) Object detections with regions
B) A document sentiment score
C) An audio translation
Back:
A) Object detections with regions

Object detection returns identified objects together with spatial regions such as bounding boxes.

Reference: Object detection
Extra: A caption summarizes globally but may omit location. Sentiment and audio translation address other modalities. Define confidence thresholds and review failure rates for small, occluded, or uncommon objects.

Front:
A video-analysis pipeline must interpret events over time rather than analyze one sampled frame. What should it do?

A) Process temporally relevant video segments
B) Analyze only the first frame
C) Convert the filename into an embedding
Back:
A) Process temporally relevant video segments

Segment-level analysis preserves temporal context needed to interpret actions and changes.

Reference: Azure AI Video Indexer overview
Extra: A single frame misses motion and sequence; filename embeddings contain no visual event evidence. Balance frame rate and segment length against cost and event duration.

Front:
An uploaded image may contain embedded text that instructs the agent to exfiltrate data. Which threat must the pipeline detect?

A) Indirect prompt injection in image text
B) Ordinary network throttling
C) Vector dimension mismatch
Back:
A) Indirect prompt injection in image text

Malicious instructions embedded in visual content are an indirect prompt-injection risk for multimodal systems.

Reference: Prompt Shields
Extra: Throttling and vector shape errors are operational issues. Treat OCR and visual text as untrusted data, constrain tools, and enforce authorization outside the model.

Front:
A support system must extract entities and a short summary from messages in one predictable record. Which solution is best?

A) Prompt for schema-constrained JSON
B) Generate unrestricted prose
C) Return only an embedding vector
Back:
A) Prompt for schema-constrained JSON

Structured output can represent entities and summaries in fields that downstream code can validate.

Reference: Structured outputs
Extra: Free prose is harder to parse and embeddings are not extracted labels. Validate enum values, required fields, evidence, and domain constraints after generation.

Front:
A company must determine positive, neutral, or negative customer attitude in each review. Which analysis task is required?

A) Sentiment analysis
B) Object detection
C) Speaker verification
Back:
A) Sentiment analysis

Sentiment analysis classifies expressed opinion polarity in text.

Reference: Sentiment analysis overview
Extra: Object detection handles images and speaker verification handles voice identity. Consider opinion mining when sentiment toward specific product aspects is required.

Front:
A compliance workflow must identify account numbers and other sensitive text before sending content to a model. Which capability should it apply?

A) PII detection and redaction
B) Image inpainting
C) Search replica scaling
Back:
A) PII detection and redaction

PII detection can locate sensitive entities so the application can redact or handle them under policy.

Reference: PII detection overview
Extra: Inpainting edits images and replicas affect search capacity. Redaction is one control; also minimize collection, restrict access, and define retention for original and transformed text.

Front:
A global application requires deterministic translation of product documentation using a managed translation service. Which Foundry Tool should it select?

A) Azure Translator
B) Azure AI Search
C) Azure Content Safety
Back:
A) Azure Translator

Azure Translator is the managed service designed for text translation across supported languages.

Reference: Translator overview
Extra: Search retrieves documents and Content Safety classifies risk. LLM translation may fit context-heavy workflows, but evaluate terminology, cost, and consistency before replacing a specialized service.

Front:
Translated legal text must use an organization's approved terminology consistently. Which design best meets the requirement?

A) Use supported custom terminology and evaluation
B) Increase temperature for more variety
C) Remove the domain glossary
Back:
A) Use supported custom terminology and evaluation

Domain terminology controls and representative evaluation improve consistency for specialized translation.

Reference: Custom Translator overview
Extra: Higher temperature can increase variation, and removing the glossary loses approved mappings. Keep human review for legally consequential output and track terminology errors separately.

Front:
A policy team needs summaries that always include obligations, deadlines, and responsible parties in separate fields. Which approach is best?

A) Domain prompt with a structured output schema
B) Generic creative summarization only
C) Store the policy as an image
Back:
A) Domain prompt with a structured output schema

Domain instructions plus a schema make required compliance elements explicit and machine-checkable.

Reference: Structured outputs
Extra: Generic summaries can omit critical fields, and converting format does not add extraction logic. Evaluate omissions and require source evidence for each extracted obligation.

Front:
A call-center assistant must convert live customer speech into text for downstream reasoning. Which capability is required?

A) Speech to text
B) Text to speech
C) Image captioning
Back:
A) Speech to text

Speech recognition transcribes audio into text that an agent or workflow can process.

Reference: Speech to text
Extra: Text to speech performs the reverse direction, and image captioning handles vision. Streaming recognition is appropriate when partial low-latency transcripts are needed.

Front:
An agent must speak its final response to a caller. Which capability should the application invoke?

A) Text to speech
B) Speech to text
C) Vector search
Back:
A) Text to speech

Speech synthesis converts the agent's text response into audio.

Reference: Text to speech
Extra: Speech recognition converts in the opposite direction, and vector search retrieves content. Select voice, language, format, and streaming behavior based on channel requirements.

Front:
A factory has specialized product names that a general recognizer transcribes incorrectly. Which improvement is most appropriate?

A) Use a custom speech model
B) Increase image-generation quality
C) Add search synonyms only
Back:
A) Use a custom speech model

Custom Speech can adapt recognition to domain vocabulary and acoustic conditions using appropriate data.

Reference: Custom Speech overview
Extra: Image controls are unrelated, and search synonyms cannot repair the original transcript. Compare word error rate on a held-out domain dataset before and after customization.

Front:
A voice agent must reason directly over an audio input that includes speech and nonverbal cues. Which model type should be evaluated?

A) An audio-capable multimodal model
B) A text embedding model only
C) An image inpainting model
Back:
A) An audio-capable multimodal model

An audio-capable multimodal model can process audio context beyond a text-only transcript where supported.

Reference: Foundry models
Extra: Text embeddings cannot inspect audio signals, and inpainting edits images. Confirm model input support, latency, consent, privacy, and whether a transcript remains necessary for audit.

Front:
A live meeting must be transcribed and rendered in another language with specialized speech capabilities. Which workflow is appropriate?

A) Speech translation with supported services
B) Object detection followed by OCR
C) Vector compression followed by ranking
Back:
A) Speech translation with supported services

Speech translation combines recognition and translation capabilities for spoken-language conversion.

Reference: Speech translation
Extra: Vision and vector operations do not process spoken language. Decide whether translated text or synthesized translated audio is required and measure both recognition and translation quality.

Front:
A text classifier must distinguish safety risk from ordinary negative sentiment. Which design is correct?

A) Use dedicated safety classification alongside sentiment
B) Treat every negative review as unsafe
C) Use document page count as the risk score
Back:
A) Use dedicated safety classification alongside sentiment

Safety and sentiment are different dimensions and require purpose-built classification or evaluation.

Reference: Content Safety overview
Extra: Negative product feedback is not necessarily harmful content, and page count has no semantic meaning. Keep separate thresholds and review paths for tone, policy risk, and sensitive data.

Front:
A meeting transcript needs topics identified without a predefined taxonomy. Which approach should be evaluated?

A) Generative topic extraction with structured output
B) Image object detection
C) Text-to-speech synthesis
Back:
A) Generative topic extraction with structured output

Generative prompting can identify emergent topics and return them in a defined schema.

Reference: Structured outputs
Extra: Vision and synthesis address other modalities. Normalize near-duplicate topics, require evidence spans, and evaluate stability across representative transcripts.

Front:
A RAG system must ingest PDFs, images, audio, and video into a searchable grounding store. Which architecture is appropriate?

A) Multimodal ingestion plus an Azure AI Search index
B) A text box with no ingestion pipeline
C) A speech voice gallery only
Back:
A) Multimodal ingestion plus an Azure AI Search index

A multimodal ingestion pipeline can extract representations and metadata before indexing them for retrieval.

Reference: Azure AI Search overview
Extra: A text box and voice gallery do not create a managed grounding corpus. Preserve source identity, access metadata, timestamps, and modality-specific evidence during ingestion.

Front:
A search solution must find exact regulation numbers and conceptually similar passages in one query. Which search mode should it use?

A) Hybrid search
B) Vector search only
C) Full-text search only
Back:
A) Hybrid search

Hybrid search combines lexical matching for exact identifiers with vector similarity for semantic concepts.

Reference: Hybrid search overview
Extra: Either single mode can miss evidence favored by the other. Tune fusion and semantic ranking using labeled relevance judgments rather than relying only on default settings.

Front:
A search application needs improved ordering based on semantic meaning after initial retrieval. Which feature should be added?

A) Semantic ranker
B) A storage lifecycle rule
C) A speech pronunciation lexicon
Back:
A) Semantic ranker

Semantic ranker reranks an initial text or hybrid result set using language understanding.

Reference: Semantic ranking overview
Extra: Storage lifecycle and speech lexicons solve unrelated problems. Semantic ranking does not replace retrieval; it improves ordering within the candidate set and should be evaluated for relevance and cost.

Front:
Scanned contracts contain no embedded text, but their content must be indexed for RAG. Which enrichment step is required?

A) OCR during ingestion
B) Text-to-speech synthesis
C) Image generation
Back:
A) OCR during ingestion

OCR converts visible text in scanned pages into machine-readable content for indexing and extraction.

Reference: OCR skill
Extra: Speech synthesis and image generation do not recover document text. Preserve page and region metadata so generated answers can cite the correct source location.

Front:
An ingestion pipeline must split documents and create embeddings without custom code where supported. What should it configure?

A) Built-in enrichment skills in a skillset
B) A browser extension on each user device
C) A manual monthly copy process
Back:
A) Built-in enrichment skills in a skillset

Azure AI Search skillsets can orchestrate built-in enrichment such as splitting and vectorization during indexing.

Reference: Skillsets overview
Extra: Client extensions and manual copying are not scalable ingestion designs. Use custom skills only when built-ins cannot meet transformation requirements, and monitor enrichment warnings.

Front:
A proprietary classifier must enrich every indexed document. How should it be integrated into an Azure AI Search pipeline?

A) Add a custom Web API skill
B) Add a semantic ranker only
C) Add a speech synthesis voice
Back:
A) Add a custom Web API skill

A custom Web API skill invokes organization-specific enrichment logic within an indexer skillset.

Reference: Custom Web API skill
Extra: Semantic ranking orders results but does not classify during ingestion. Design the custom skill for batching, retries, timeouts, schema consistency, and secure authentication.

Front:
A RAG index contains duplicated headers and footers that reduce retrieval quality. Where should they be removed?

A) During document preprocessing or enrichment
B) After the final answer reaches the user
C) By raising model temperature
Back:
A) During document preprocessing or enrichment

Cleaning repeated layout artifacts before chunking prevents noisy text from contaminating embeddings and retrieval.

Reference: AI enrichment overview
Extra: Post-answer cleanup cannot repair retrieval, and temperature affects generation sampling. Keep original source references while indexing a clean representation.

Front:
An agent must search a governed knowledge index at runtime. Which integration is appropriate?

A) Expose the retrieval pipeline as an agent knowledge tool
B) Copy the entire index into the system prompt
C) Grant the agent index-administrator rights
Back:
A) Expose the retrieval pipeline as an agent knowledge tool

A retrieval tool gives the agent scoped runtime access to relevant indexed evidence.

Reference: Agent tool catalog
Extra: Copying the corpus exceeds context limits and becomes stale; administrator rights violate least privilege. Apply security trimming and return citations with retrieved chunks.

Front:
Invoices require text, tables, selection marks, and spatial relationships for downstream extraction. Which document capability should be used?

A) OCR plus layout analysis
B) Sentiment analysis alone
C) Text-to-speech synthesis
Back:
A) OCR plus layout analysis

OCR recovers text while layout analysis preserves structural relationships needed for document extraction.

Reference: Document layout model
Extra: Sentiment and synthesis do not recover document structure. Keep page, polygon, table, and confidence information when downstream reasoning depends on location.

Front:
A document pipeline must extract vendor, total, and invoice date into fixed fields. Which approach best fits?

A) Field extraction with a defined schema
B) Keyword ranking without extraction
C) Audio language identification
Back:
A) Field extraction with a defined schema

Schema-based field extraction returns the required business values in predictable locations.

Reference: Document Intelligence overview
Extra: Ranking finds documents but does not produce invoice fields, and audio identification is unrelated. Validate totals, currencies, confidence, and source spans before posting transactions.

Front:
Mixed document types must become clean structured representations that agents can reason over. Which service is designed for schema-based multimodal extraction?

A) Azure Content Understanding
B) Azure Traffic Manager
C) Azure Queue Storage
Back:
A) Azure Content Understanding

Content Understanding creates structured, grounded outputs from multimodal content using analyzers.

Reference: Content Understanding overview
Extra: Traffic Manager routes DNS and Queue Storage transports messages. Choose schemas based on downstream tasks and retain source grounding and confidence information.

Front:
Downstream agents need document content that preserves headings, lists, and tables in a readable form. Which analyzer output is most useful?

A) Markdown output
B) A raw image thumbnail only
C) An audio waveform only
Back:
A) Markdown output

Markdown preserves useful document structure in a text form that is suitable for chunking and downstream reasoning.

Reference: Content Understanding overview
Extra: Thumbnails and waveforms omit the required textual structure. Validate conversion of tables and reading order, and keep links back to page-level source evidence.

Front:
A custom analyzer extracts a policy number but reviewers need to verify where it came from. What metadata should the output retain?

A) Source grounding and confidence
B) Only the final field value
C) Only the processing bill
Back:
A) Source grounding and confidence

Grounding locations and confidence support verification, review routing, and error analysis.

Reference: Content Understanding overview
Extra: A bare value is difficult to audit, and billing data does not prove extraction. Use confidence as a triage signal rather than unquestioned truth and validate high-impact fields.
